question: Does higher reasoning effort improve quality enough to pay for the extra output tokens?
setup: 6 planning/orchestration tasks (plan, delegation brief with a child cap, debug triage, cost judgment, 3-way choice, verify before reporting) x 3 effort levels (low, medium, high) x 2 runs x 3 models = 108 runs, one-shot, no tools. kimi and deepseek ran first (72 runs); glm was added later with the same tasks and grader (36 runs). Pass counts here are from one grader, openai/gpt-6-luna (not a candidate), in batched calls with anonymized, shuffled answers. e08b-three-graders.json re-grades the same answers with two more graders.

cost.total_note: total_usd_est covers kimi, deepseek and the luna grader; glm adds 0.0157.
cost.passed_note: passed and cost_per_pass use the luna-only pass counts above.

finding: No effort level buys a clear quality win: pass counts show no consistent low < medium < high trend (deepseek peaks at medium 7/12 then drops to 3/12 at high; kimi low and medium tie at 5). x: kimi at low is its most verbose (mean 1,079 output tokens). Under luna alone, cost per passed task is kimi $0.0129, deepseek $0.0015, glm $0.0009. Under the majority of three graders (e08b-three-graders.json) kimi passes 29/36 ($0.0075 per pass), deepseek 16/36 ($0.0013, contaminated: one grader is deepseek-v4-pro) and glm 17/36 ($0.0009). The quality ranking depends on the grader; glm has the lowest cost per pass under both.
limitations: task 3 (debug triage) failed in every cell under luna, likely grader strictness
letter-parsing of grader output is approximate
notes: Models were called through an OpenAI-compatible router; names and prices are as recorded at run time.
